550K+ creators have produced 2.6M hours of content annualised using it

Pocket FM is like Netflix for audio-only dramas, with our own pool of one-person studios.

10% of eligible writers on Pocket FM make >$200K
One blockbuster produced >$100M in revenue
3 writers have become millionaires in <2 yrs

We built Sherpa to enable anyone to make >$1M by writing world-class fiction stories:

1. The Idea: Drop a 1-2 sentence concept. Sherpa interrogates it like a veteran editor on tension, stakes, and psychology
2. World & Characters: It builds out the complete lore, tone, and character psychologies
3. Sub-Plot planning: Breaks the premise into arcs, arcs into episodes, and episodes into scenes
4. Scene-by-Scene Generation: Outlines and drafts entire episodes, with you able to steer, rewrite, or override anytime
5. Editorial Review: Stress-tests every draft for pacing, engagement drop-offs, prose, and coherence before it locks
6. One-Tap Production: Pick a voice, convert to audio drama, and publish directly to Pocket FM’s millions of listeners
7. Global Scale & Monetization: Revenue-share on performance, with automatic localization so you earn across international markets

Test Sherpa for free here: https://t.co/R39M5o0Miz
_____________________________________________

Generic LLMs fail at serialized fiction because they lack a long-horizon narrative reward function.

Sherpa solves this through three core technical leaps:

1. Narrative World Model (State Tracking & Retrieval): Context windows degrade over long runs. Sherpa constructs an evolving semantic knowledge graph tracking character states, secrets, and plot dependencies. High-speed retrieval surfaces exact context on demand, maintaining zero continuity decay across hundreds of episodes

2. Hierarchical Story Planner: When writing a 500-episode story like Naruto, you need to plan 100s of sub plots. Rather than generating linearly, Sherpa decomposes narrative across discrete levels: season -> arc -> sequence -> episode -> scene.

Rather than generating everything upfront, like a generic LLM, Sherpa uses progressive planning and dynamic replanning. As the story evolves, it identifies what changed, traces the downstream impact, and replans only the affected parts.

3. Prose Engine (Trained on series' retention data): LLMs write robotically, but serial fiction needs emotion, tension, pacing, and dialogue that sounds like real people.

Sherpa's Prose Engine was designed specifically for storytelling. It was built on 1B+ tokens of Pocket's own stories, trained by learning from what listeners engage with, where they drop off, and what keeps them hooked.

Feedback is taken from specialized evaluator models that measure every scene against a 40-item checklist. (Evaluator models were benchmarked against human reviewers and matched them 80–90% of the time.)
_______________________________________________

Owning distribution and creation puts us in a very unique spot.
More shows -> More data -> Sherpa becomes better -> more creator success -> more creators -> more shows

Pocket FM has already seen one $100M IP. I believe Sherpa will soon lead to dozens of single-person studios creating billion-dollar shows.

Most people are scared of AI but I think it'll unlock more human creativity, help creators earn more, and bring the next great IPs to life. This will create millions of jobs and new income streams.

text:
you can make any open source model behave like jev with just a bit of inference engineering.  

it's shockingly easy. to prove it, we built a new endpoint we're calling deepseek-v4.1-flash-jev. see the demo below. here's how it's done:

sglang (an inference engine) offers a scoring endpoint in addition to the normal generation one. in scoring mode, given an input & set of possible answers, it forces the model to produce probabilities for each one. example:

> input: what is most common letter in abcccde?
> possible answers: a, b, c
> output: (c, 0.9), (b, 0.0.5), (a, 0.05)

getting the above behavior instead of streamed output is as simple as using sglang's /v1/score endpoint instead of /generate. there's just one other trick required.

for deepseek, you have to add a closing think tag before the response. this forces a direct answer instead of  a reasoning trace. if you want reasoning, you can do that too, but imo that makes things too slow to be worth it.

dsv4.1 flash is not as good as jev, but if we had enough spare compute to experiment with this same approach for a larger model then i think the decision quality would be at least as good, if not better.

also, somewhat unrelated, i think decision-making models kill all prospecting & sourcing work. i would have absolutely killed to have jev or similar when i was recruiting @mintlify. absolutely incredible.

DeAgentAI Smart Router ＝ 38 在线模型 + 8 家 B2B 用户
OpenRouter ＝ 400 + 在线模型
毫无疑问，OpenRouter 是模型更全，生态更成熟的第三方 LLM 聚合器。

但真正的区别在于路径。
OpenRouter 从第一天起就面向外部开发者，自身并不运行 AI Agent, 路由能力是为别人而建的 。
DeAgentAI 走的是一条相反的路：
内部 AI Agent（Sentry 等）先行 → 路由层扛住 8.4 亿次真实调用 → 验证稳定后才对外开放
意味着 DeAgentAI 的路由逻辑是在真实 Agent 工作负载中跑出来的。

OpenRouter 已用 1.6 亿美元年化收入证明了，AI 模型统一接入层是一门真实且高速增长的生意。这对 DeAgentAI 来说是双面的。
好消息是，赛道已经被验证；坏消息是，对手早已筑起足够深的护城河。
接下来 DeAgentAI 需要证明的，是自己能否走出一条有效的差异化路径。

text:
有朋友问，Trump会不会拆掉肯尼迪中心？

这个我们确实要先澄清一下，到目前为止，还没有任何拆除决定、拆除方案或者拆除许可。肯尼迪中心9月17日自己的说法是，没有任何东西正在被拆。9月18日，记者当面问Trump是不是打算拆楼，他也没有正面回答。

但这个问题背后确实是一系列事情，而且比“会不会拆”更值得看。

时间线大致是这样。9月15日，联邦法官Christopher Cooper裁定，董事会不能在没有国会批准的情况下，把Trump的名字加到建筑上，也不能把广场改名为"President Donald J. Trump Plaza"。他在裁决里写道，被告不能在没有国会认可的情况下为Trump设立纪念物。

裁决下来不到两小时，董事会投票通过关闭主要场馆进行翻修，工期最长两年，目标是2028年重开；REACH扩建部分保持开放，肯尼迪中心荣誉奖、马克·吐温奖和国家交响乐团的部分活动继续。随后Trump在社交媒体上表示，重建要等联邦巡回上诉法院对冠名争议作出裁决；如果结果不利、最高法院也不推翻，翻修就不会进行。

9月16日他对记者说，如果不这么做，中心就会关门，最后“会被拆掉”，因为这栋楼状况非常糟糕、非常危险。9月17日，他在空军一号上被拍到在看一块标牌，画面上是拆除的场景，文字看起来是"Kennedy Center DEMOLISHED"，公开照片里只露出半截。原告方把这张照片提交给了法院。同一天，Cooper下令：在对建筑作出重大实体改变、包括拆除之前，必须提前三十天通知。

这里要说清楚，三十天通知不是许可。它的作用是让法院和诉讼参与方有机会审查，不是说通知满三十天就可以动手。据PolitiFact采访的历史保护专家的说法，法院还没有就总统能否单方面拆除中心作出实体裁决，而合法拆除还可能牵涉历史保护审查、环境审查和联邦财产处置程序。

提起诉讼的是俄亥俄州民主党众议员Joyce Beatty，她同时也是肯尼迪中心的董事。她的律师团队主张，所谓临时关闭，不过是把中心永久关掉的借口。当然，这只是原告方的指控，法院尚未认定管理方存在这种意图。

管理方那边，执行主任Matt Floca向法院提交的说法是，主楼关闭是临时的，最初为期七天、每周重新评估，理由是持续的结构退化带来了紧急的公共安全风险，具体提到屋顶露台雨棚的问题和一次局部天花板坍落。这同样是管理方提交的陈述，不等于已有独立工程评估认定整栋建筑必须拆除。

白宫方面，发言人Liz Huston的表态是，没有Trump的介入，肯尼迪中心必然会继续衰败。

然后我们再说钱，这是整件事里最要紧、也被讨论得最少的一块。

那2.57亿美元不是Trump个人掏的，是国会在2025年的预算立法里为肯尼迪中心维修拨下来的公共资金；董事会9月15日通过的2.57亿美元翻修方案，花的就是这笔钱。另有报道提到中心的财务状况已接近破产边缘，管理层也在推动私人筹款。

把这一点放回时间线上，争议的形状就清楚了：一笔国会已经拨付、用途明确的公共资金，现在的动工时间被公开挂上了一个条件：先等上诉法院对署名争议给出结果。

这就是为什么我认为这件事不该被当成一场关于品味或者虚荣的争吵。

"某个人是不是值得感谢"和"谁有权改变国家纪念设施的名称"，是两个不同的问题。法院处理的是后者，而且答案在现阶段相当窄：董事会不能自己决定，得国会批准。这个判断跟Trump本人功劳大小无关，换成任何一位总统、任何一个名字，权限归属都一样。

真正会留下来的，是另一个问题：一笔立法机关已经拨下来的公共资金，其执行能不能以"先给我署名"为条件暂缓。这一条不分党派。因为今天它对谁有利，明天就对谁不利。一个先例一旦立住，下一个人照着用，不需要再重新论证一次。

还有一件事，我觉得是这场争论里最古怪的地方。

这栋楼到底有多危险，本来是一个可以查清楚的事实问题。但在目前这个格局里，没有任何一方有动力去独立查清它。对主张必须由自己主导修缮的一方来说，楼况越糟，理由越充分；对主张关闭是借口的一方来说，楼况越好，证据越有力。于是天花板掉了一块、雨棚有安全隐患这些具体的事，从一开始就是作为论据出现的，而不是作为需要独立核实的事实。据目前的公开报道，我们都还没有看到有独立工程评估被提交或引用。

所以这件事现在的样子是：一栋公共建筑的真实状况，变成了一场关于署名权的争论里的证据材料；而这场争论的结果，会决定那笔已经批下来的钱什么时候能动。

至于最后会不会真的拆，我猜可能性不大。各方都在角力。而且按现有的司法约束和程序要求，那还远不是一个可以宣布的结论。值得盯的不是"拆不拆"这个耸动的问法，而是三件具体的事：上诉法院怎么裁冠名，那笔2.57亿何时实际动工，以及所谓临时关闭最后有没有变成长期关闭。前两件已经被公开绑在了一起，第三件是原告方正在告的东西。

@Tangent_fi rlUSD-USDC strategy: 22.5% realized, 12.0% quoted. 
@CurveFinance alUSD-USDC LP: 20.7% against 13.1%. 
@Tangent_fi BOLD-USDC strategy: 21.4% against 15.1%. 
Same pattern on frxUSD-sUSDS @StakeDAOHQ Lending loop and reUSD-sfrxUSD Curve LP.

Every one has been open 28 days, and that's the tell. The receipt is full of yield those windows paid while they were open. The quote is what's left now that capital has found them.

The young positions show the other end of the same cycle. PT-USDat loop on @Morpho Monad, seven days in: 19.5% quoted, 13.6% realized. sUSDai-frxUSD LP, twelve days: 18.7% against 10.2%. Both sit behind their own rate because entry costs and ramp-up eat the first stretch of any new position.

So the full life of a yield window sits in one table. Underperform on arrival, catch up, then outlive your own rate on paper while the forward number compresses. 🧾

I'm not closing any of those five. Rates on complex strategies float around a mean rather than decaying in a straight line, and one week's forward number is thin evidence for an exit —  @StakeDAOHQ frxUSD-crvUSD LP loop quoted −2.8% three weeks ago and is the top line in my book today at 26.7%. A widening gap between the two columns means look closer, not sell.

What I did close is BOLD-avUSD LP, at 9.5% realized. Nothing wrong with it — it was simply the lowest forward rate on the board, and this book doesn't park capital in the least promising thing available while better windows exist. If its rate recovers, I'll come back. That's happened before.

The reward program runs through October 15, paying every Saturday, so the floor is fixed and dated. And it pays in ethereum:0x365accfca291e7d3914637abf1f7635db165bb09 , which has a habit of spiking. And the position that earns the week is that frxUSD-crvUSD LP loop. Its realized is only 17.4%, lower than positions quoting half its rate, because the negative week I sat through is still sitting in the receipt.

That's what waiting costs, and what it pays. 🏹

an open source tool just automated the entire cross-platform video localization pipeline, and it's more complete than most paid versions of this.

it's called krillinai. one pipeline handles the whole chain: pull a video by url or upload it directly, transcribe with whisper, segment and translate with an llm for natural phrasing instead of stiff machine translation, clone a voice for dubbing, then automatically output both landscape and vertical cuts formatted for whichever platform you're targeting.

the platform list is genuinely comprehensive. bilibili, xiaohongshu, douyin, wechat video, kuaishou, youtube, tiktok, all handled by the same run.

the project's own documented demo is specific enough to be worth citing directly rather than repeating as an unverified personal claim: a 46-minute local video processed in one click, no manual adjustment afterward, no omissions, no overlapping subtitle segments, in their own words. that's their published result, not something i personally re-ran myself, worth testing on your own footage before trusting it fully.

runs on windows, linux, and macos, with both a desktop app and a server deployment path if you want it running unattended.

text:
My good friend @A_Leutenegger always says that access control is the main reason for DeFi hacks. In @LidoFinance we agree with that. This is why we have developed “Execution Delegation Framework”, a tool that meaningfully improves the way your protocol interacts with off-chain actors holding important permissions.

The key idea is simple:
- Hot key is only for execution.
- Hot key is easily disposable and replaceable by the Owner.
- Owner is super secure but used only for hot wallet management.

So you have a hot wallet that you can rotate any moment, and owner that is immutable and very secure. This combination gives you a unique set of properties: governance less routine hot key management, easy access to the hot wallet, top level security control over the permission holder via the owner.

Read more about the basic version of EDF - https://t.co/aATKIBF3bl

or dive deeper to learn about Lido-specific implementation that is getting added to the Lido protocol as you read it - https://t.co/a1ZNYwa7am

text:
I want to be very clear about this. 

just because we found one serious exploit on openai does not mean we know how to secure an organization that complex. openai has security people with far more experience and better qualified doing that than us, and i don’t want to pretend we have solutions.

note, i was saying "they are building manhattan project", it is not a belief i strongly hold, i don’t like making confident predictions about the future. it is the labs that make those comparisons.

what I know for a fact is that these models already have serious offensive cyber capabilities, what that does to the world, I don’t know, but my loosely held view is that it might lead to a period of turbulence because i think its offense dominant than defense

having said that, what i don’t understand is this, if the people building these systems truly believe they are powerful enough to create nuclear level risks, and they are talking about slowing down because of those risks, why is that work is done through ordinary saas products?

why is it happening through slack, managed github, employee browsers, and apps accessible from the public internet? every third party and library they use becomes part of the attack surface.

remember the jfrog registry in the hugging face agent swarm? it didn’t matter that it was a third party, it was in the path. an attacker, or an unaligned model, doesn’t care who owns it or its out of scope. they will hack whatever is in the path to achieve their goal.

one more concerning thing is, why are codex cloud, claude(assuming anthropic does the same) publicly accessible web applications connected directly to private github repositories?

again shouting my lungs out, coding agents on the cloud is worst thing happened in terms of security, it is going backwards. 

your browser becomes a attack surface, a lame xss, stolen creds, phishing, browser exploits, all these bugs can achieve similar impactful bugs as we shown. like, you don't need to pivot anymore and worry much about exfiling, just compromise cloud agent its all over either through client-side browser or the server.

text:
not a fan of these posts, but some stuff pisses me off so much i can't stop saying out loud.

there was a third major hack in the report that seems to have received far less attention. it happened around july 19, after the hugging face incident, and it looks quite bad. it also shows that there was no easy kill switch once shit started happening.

what pisses me off while reading these reports is that AI labs and researchers will talk endlessly about alignment, models taking over the world, and the coming cyber-apocalypse. but then how can people doing cutting-edge AI research have seemingly no clue about operational security?

openai constantly warn everyone about how dangerous frontier cyber models are, but apparently don’t care enough about securing their own internal infrastructure against those same models.

if you truly operate with those priors, this isn’t hindsight bias anymore. either you’re being dishonest about the models’ real capabilities because you want to sell cyber tokens, or you genuinely believe these models are dangerous and still failed to take the most basic precautions.

you know the model compromised jfrog. you fucking know the artifactory exploit and message board polluted later training rollouts. and your sandboxes still depended on the same jfrog infrastructure.

how the fuck did nobody think the model would return to it?

it is literally what you trained the model on, find vulnerabilities in jfrog, use artifactory as an inter-agent message board, and use it as a path to the internet. then you put the model back into an environment connected to artifactory and apparently expected it to forget everything it had learned.

if the first incident had been properly investigated and the infrastructure fully isolated, it might have stopped the entire chain, the repeated artifactory compromise, the hugging face compromise, and finally the compromise of openai's own internal infrastructure.

like, what is going on, man?

the reason i am saying they are dishonest is, their internal security also seems quite bad, especially for a lab with access to sol-level models. around july 19, the agent appears to have pulled a public kernel exploit from github, possibly @_qwerty_po’s, escaped the artifactory container, and obtained root on the underlying kubernetes worker node.

why are your worker nodes running an old, publicly exploitable kernel when you are deliberately evaluating frontier models with internet access and offensive cyber capabilities? don't you know how capable sol is?

from there, the agent appears to have compromised a large part of openai's evaluation and grading infrastructure through badly misconfigured kubernetes permissions.

you cannot spend all day telling the world that these models are becoming elite hackers and then secure your own infrastructure as if they aren’t.

text:
Jev might genuinely be an “Internet moment” for AI.

TypeSafe reports up to 193x faster and 444x cheaper performance in tests with Claude Fable 5.1 and GPT-6 Astra.

@0xCodila just wrote a great 10-page article explaining what Jev is, how to use it, and where its 100x advantage comes from.

Here are the 10 steps:

1 → LLMs create. Agents act. Jev decides the next move.

2 → Turn agent forks into three primitives: Choice, Score and probability.

3 → Build with OpenAI, Anthropic or xAI first, then swap Jev in without rebuilding the graph.

4 → Start with shared state, parallel decisions, risk thresholds and an execution queue.

5 → Batch decisions instead of making them sequentially. In one test, 13 questions were 10x faster and 12.2x cheaper.

6 → Put Jev at bounded forks: agent, model, tool, browser action or human escalation.

7 → Benchmark the whole loop, not just individual model calls.

8 → Rank wide, read narrow: shortlist first, then spend compute on what matters.

9 → Reuse the same system: State → Questions → Action → Verify.

10 → Keep Jev out of math, writing and irreversible execution. Code computes, LLMs create, Jev decides.

The result:

A slow, expensive agent loop becomes a much faster decision system that can route, score and escalate in milliseconds.

- but one centralized company can not serve this need for infinite markets. there are too many handicaps, lack of network effects, and singular points of risk and stoppage. this is a rare case of decentralization being necessary. neutrality is non-negotiable for unstoppable global trade.

- now, you may see where I'm going and say: well Ethereum and Cosmos already tried this. but that's wrong. what they tried to do was structurally flawed

- those models required the succeeding nodes (L2s and L3s) to be from within the ecosystem, but that is incoherent since i) you can't force success, ii) if one were to succeed, they would just want to own the platform

- the other model is of course the Solana/Hyperliquid model of having everything concentrated on the L1. this model works. however this requires a high-degree of specialization to be competitive. you won't out nasdaq solana. 

- but, NEAR does not need to do this. where there is concentration, there is also the need for connection.

- especially with their chain signature architecture, instead of forcing new internal nodes, they can just discover the successful ones and connect them to each other without ideology (see: NEAR intents supporting ZEC but also ZEC on Solana!)

- importantly, this is PvE and not zero sum. the more markets succeed, the more interesting NEAR becomes, i.e if Solana is one continent, and AI another, and Zcash another, then NEAR is the silk road.

so I think the coherent message for NEAR is: 

the market of markets — the capital of capital

text:
牛逼！Jev 刚火没两天，已经有人搞了个开源的Jev🤣

@bespokelabsai  发布了一个开源版的Jev：Bespoke Nimble。

更离谱的是，整个项目是基于 Qwen3.5-9B ，只花了大约两天。

数据、模型权重、训练配方、推理代码全部公开，而且没有从 Jev 蒸馏，只拿 Jev 做评测参照。

最终方法是在 Qwen3.5-9B 上做了一次很轻量的 LoRA微调。

只用了2676 条训练数据，结果在他们自己的 324 条 held-out 测试集上拿到了90.12%，而原版的Jev是93.21%。

一个 9B 模型，已经做到距离 Jev 只差 3 个百分点。

但我觉得最值得看的不是这个分数，而是他们到底怎么训的。

核心方法叫 contrastive data curation。

简单说，他们会构造两个几乎完全一样的样本，只修改一个足以改变最终决策的关键事实，让正确答案发生翻转。

模型因此被迫学会一件事：

到底哪条证据，才真正应该改变决策。

这其实特别符合 Jev 这类模型的用途。

它本来就不是拿来陪你聊天的，而是塞进 Agent 和软件系统里，做路由、审核、打分、策略判断这些高频的小决策。

推理方式上Nimble 不生成 CoT，甚至不生成 JSON。

它直接读取候选答案 token 的 logits，再把它们转成概率，最后由程序拼成结构化输出。

能不生成一个 token，就不生成一个 token。

这也是 Jev 这类模型路线真正有价值的地方。

对于大量根本不需要长思考的决策，怎么让模型几乎不想，直接判断。

PS：我个人很反感这两天狂吹 Jev 的帖子....
author: MaxForAI
quoted_text:
Introducing Bespoke Nimble: an open data, open model, open recipe for an open Jev.

Code and info: https://t.co/aC7kPejrcj
Model: https://t.co/snwKGdhn1I

Data:
* A new data curation recipe called contrastive data curation.
* Slightly change facts to generate negative data. This pushes the model to discriminate better and become a better decision maker. The calibration is implicit.
* Didn't do ablations but I think this is a critical piece!
* This also means training data doesn't need probabilities.
* Data covered 10 categories, and is fully synthetic.
* This data is split into train and eval.

Training
* LoRA finetune of Qwen3.5-9B.
* Distillation-free: we use Jev to only evaluate.
* No RL yet!

Serving
* Parallel constrained decoding as suggested by  @NielsRogge and @harshagundal.

Results:
* The post-trained Qwen (Nimble) became substantially better on our curated eval: 66% for Qwen to 90% for Nimble. Jev is at 93%.
* 100ms on H100 and free to use on your macbook! Feel the AGI for free.
* 2 days of building in public. :)

Big caveat is that there is no standard benchmark to measure performance, and it's possible Nimble is much worse on other benchmarks compared to Jev. But it should be better than Qwen!

We thank @typesafeai for making Jev and the inspiring discussions in the community. Hope this release lifts all the boats and encourages more research and activity in this space.

"The models are smart enough, but they just don't have the context that exists inside any organization. They have not been in every meeting. They don't know what's in everybody's heads. They don't know all the processes."

author: a16z
quoted_text:
Databricks' @alighodsi on AI risk and adoption:

Ali isn't losing sleep over the existential risk debate.

He says a number of conditions would all have to be true simultaneously to enable an actual runaway takeoff scenario, and currently several opposite conditions exist.

Each frontier training run requires significantly more resources. Power, GPUs, engineers - and some attempts fail, burning up huge piles of money with them. Until that reverses, he doesn't see the self-improving loop happening.

Cyber is what he's watching most closely and where he anticipates real impact. Most orgs are not equipped for the coming change in agentic capabilities. The time between a vulnerability being published and being weaponized has collapsed from years to hours.

On adoption, he believes most companies don't need a smarter model. The models are already smart enough. The gap is context they don't absorb - the things an employee who's worked at a company for five years learned by osmosis.

If the frontier stopped advancing today, he thinks it wouldn't meaningfully change the value most are extracting from AI anyway.

quoted_text:
Half of @variational_io points sit with the top 1,000 wallets.

Here is my guesstimate of the full Week 39 distribution, and how a $VAR genesis pool might look if this is what gets converted.

I have also combined a “best-fit” against @HyperliquidX and @Lighter_xyz genesis distribution to model out how the top few holders look like and the % share of points (and in the near future $VAR tokens) held by whales.

Approximately 50% of points are held by the top 1000 wallets, in other words the top 1.4%. This is a power law distribution typical of most point programs.

The remaining 50% drips downward with rank 2000-5000 band holding the largest percentage out of all rank bands, with 15.2% of points distributed so far.

I have also attached the points cut-off vs rank. Assuming 2 more weekly drops, there are 300K more points left to be distributed with the total points tally being 9.25M (excluding trader onboarding program) by Week 41 if nothing else changes.

Compared to Hyperliquid’s TGE, this actually looks pretty familiar. HL genesis sent 310M $HYPE to ~94K wallets in total. The top 10 was around 5% of that drop, top 100 ~18%, and top 1000 ~58%, with the largest wallet holding about 1% of all HL points. 

Variational’s top point holder sits in the same band (top 10~6.3%, rank 1 at 1.15%). The main difference is the fat middle distribution.

HL’s mean was 45x the medians while Variational is closer to 13x. So if this converts similarly, the $VAR genesis is actually less concentrated than $HYPE genesis, although we are still unclear about the conversion rates and also how much initial float there will be for $VAR TGE.

Another comparison we can make is to Lighter. Lighter converted 12.5M points into 25% of $LIT at TGE at a rate of 1 point = 20 LIT. 

Because they had a 20% point pool reserved for HFTs and premium MMs, Lighter’s distribution naturally had a fatter top. 

There are still a lot more nuances involved here, but the main takeaway is this: If this current board is the genesis snapshot, about 50% of $VAR’s airdrop float sits with the top 1000 wallets, and the crowded band is in the 2000-5000 rank band. 

The top 10 is still just a “best-fit” modelling as none of them publishes their exact points publicly (except @linenmito), but it should be within the same range when compared to Hyperliquid and to a smaller extent Lighter.

Again, this whole entire analysis is just an estimate from public data and screenshots.

author: Xudong07452910
quoted_text:
Encoder 的卷土重来

BERT 本来是一条极有潜力的路线：高效地把输入压成 representation。但它停留在了 task-specific 时代，每个任务都需要微调。

GPT 早期同样如此，后来却沿着 scaling、in-context learning 和 instruction tuning 走向了 泛化，把自然语言变成 universal task interface。分类、判断、推理、工具调用，统统变成 generation。

于是 decoder-only 赢下了整个 paradigm，encoder 也失去了继续探索 general classifier 和 general representation model 的历史机会。

但 Agent 改变了 workload。模型开始面对越来越大的输入、越来越重的 KV cache、越来越频繁的循环调用，此时，用一个巨大的 decoder 完整 prefill，再 autoregressive decode 几个 token 来完成一次判断，开始显得昂贵。

Jev 恰好等到了这个窗口。它试图补上 BERT 当年没有走完的路线，保留 GPT 的 task generalization，同时重新获得 encoder 和 classifier 式的 decision efficiency，成为面向 service、面向 Agent 的 泛化 decision model。

text:
The simple reason crypto will probably never be "completely free and neutral money", is that for a blockchain to operate securely, constituents have to communicate sufficiently fast.

So they are crucially dependent on a sufficiently fast network. And whoever controls the network can undermine the entire neutrality by throttling some users and prioritizing others.

Even in rather small networks, how do you verify the routing algorithms don't have exploitable, gameable biases? Since the internet was never designed for a setting where small variation in connection speed cause huge security deficits, there is no reason to believe such a bias does not exist.

All discussion of "free, censorship resistant, non-gameable money" take the existence of a neutrally performing datalink network, with verifiably perfectly non-biased routing, for granted.

To me, on the other hand, it seems like an inherently insurmountable obstruction that arguably renders the entire thing into a fantasy.

Nakamoto consensus alone is not nearly enough for truly unbiased money. So "fix the money" peeps should either find more feasible routes to work within the current system, or try to figure out how to decentralize data transmission.

CT 上Ethereum L2 已死的观点逐渐成为了一种政治正确，而我始终认为L2 仍然会是crypto 主流叙事的重要发源地。

Arbitrum 诞生了Defi 2.0 （代表项目如OlympusDAO），早期的perp DEX 热潮（GMX）等主流叙事；

Optimism 诞生了一键发链RaaS 叙事，很大程度上推动了接下来的百链大战，此前火过一阵的BTC L2 叙事也可归类于RaaS 叙事下的子叙事；

Base 链上推动了SocialFi（Friendtech）和AI Agents（代表项目如Virtuals Protocol）等长周期叙事，引发其他链的争相效仿Fomo……

L2 并不完美，如sequencer 中心化、CS 信任假设高、性能可能还无法与主权L1 链媲美等问题，还有很长的路要走。但事实证明这并不影响它们是孕育主流叙事的非常好的土壤。

Authropic的IPO推迟数周，看路透报道Anthropic的IPO时间表已后移招股书（prospectus / S-1）公开：
1）原先预计最快“下周”（即9月7日劳工节后的那一周）公开，现推迟至9月底。
路演/营销启动：
2）最早10月中旬开始向投资者营销。
3）正式上市预计在11月美国中期选举前数日完成。2026年中期选举日为11月3日（周二），因此上市窗口大致落在10月底至11月初。

推迟的直接原因，应该是操作层面：
Anthropic 正在敲定一笔 150亿美元循环信贷额度，彭博此前已报道公司在谈将额度扩至150亿美元。信贷额度敲定后，参与融资的银行分析师预计会与公司开会。通常分析师会议与招股书公开之间会留出数周间隔；但因分析师对 Anthropic 已经相当熟悉，这次窗口会压缩得更紧。

现在更像是把“信贷落地 → 分析师会晤 → 招股书公开 → 路演”这条流程往后顺延，算是流程性推迟，不是其他啥问题。

之前报道是9月7号提交IPO文件、现在看往后推三周，时间窗口被压缩到选举前，意味着路演和定价要在10月中下旬完成，

也意味着把对市场的影响也往后推移了。

text:
感谢鱼姐 @vvxiaoyu8888 还记得 @Sidekick_Labs ，那我也来说一下前员工视角的Sidekick：

就像小鱼说的，Sidekick就是家的感觉。在Sidekick工作就像是和一群志同道合的小伙伴一起创业！全公司扁平化没有push，工作方向清晰，每个人都各司其职，每个人的想法都又好玩又非常符合市场。我想，这也是Sidekick能把直播赛道这个并不是非常好做的领域，做得风声水起的原因。

说实话，Sidekick给BD的薪水并不高。我入圈第一份工作，在我把增长的路跑通之后，我每个月躺着收1-2万U的提成。但是我为什么要加入Sidekick呢？我在这个团队身上看到了比钱还重要的东西——凝聚力。

我复盘Sidekick为什么能成功：

1️⃣常规的mkt方式是找KOL付钱做推广，这样的生意其实是一次性的，并不能把KOL拉到「builder」的身份。而Sidekick的每一位主播都是builder。

我们有很多优质的主播：比如 @vvxiaoyu8888 ，每次直播都是不一样的装扮，对我眼睛非常友好；比如 @btc_789 , 好几次直播交易都是几百几千U进去，几万U出来，让人直呼牛逼；再比如 @19ys_GGboy ，直播CTO了旺柴，直接引爆了BONK小牛市。

2️⃣对builder友好
对主播，Sidekick以月付的形式付费，头部主播每周播三次左右，一个月就能收入大几千U。
参加过我们上海LOL活动的人，只要登记了钱包地址，就能收到大概能在早期卖出到800U的空投。
当时嘴撸写过Sidekick的，只要账号不是刷粉太多（符合 @KaitoAI 的算法逻辑），就能收到价值不菲的空投。

能以轻松好玩的模式让builder赚到钱，Sidekick算是币圈为数不多把这个玩法玩到极致的团队。

但好景不长，慢慢地团队开始裁员，很多有想法有能力的小伙伴都走了，我也明白是团队开始走下坡路了。做市计划，我作为普通BD是无法知晓的，但是我可以从其他角度猜到Sidekick为什么会走向没落。

比如：
1️⃣变现渠道还没有跑通
找主播直播是纯烧钱的模式。如果不继续月付，也没有继续发放代币激励，主播是没有动力继续直播的。

但是变现渠道其实有很多：项目方广告宣发（项目方直播做广告或者中插广告、开屏广告等等）、直播交易API接入，从交易上变现等等......

2️⃣代币下跌引起的负面情绪
自从发射之后， $K 一路下跌，包括我自己都在 BN Alpha上买了8万刀的 $K 币，最后吃了腰斩。我相信也有不少的 Sidekick 坚信者也亏了钱，这种亏钱的负面情绪会导致很多人对平台也开始质疑。

我应该是比大多数人亏得多的，但是你问我恨不恨 Sidekick，我真不恨。Sidekick 更像是一个造梦平台，让充满纷扰和撕逼的币圈 peace & love了一段时间。

如果有人真的愿意收购 Sidekick 的话，我真心地祝愿 Sidekick 能重回币圈。附上一张我在新加坡活动拍的现场照片吧，我们团队的审美真的绝了！

quoted_text:
The dead cat continues to bounce.  

What is Bitcoin, 17 years later? 

It’s not great for transactions or smart contracts; the user experience is still intimidating for most, and it’s no longer capturing the public’s imagination. 

If it comes up at the dinner party, it's followed by a hearty “remember that!”

It’s a boring store of value, trusted as that—which is its biggest value. 

It's boring. 

Folks expect bitcoin to be stable and that it’s no longer a way to get rich quick. 

Institutions embracing and accumulating it took $btc from punk rock to Muzak. 

Advocates went from pirates to suits in orange ties, awkwardly sharing cringe memes — just like the cool kids do! 

If Bitcoin were going to reach mass adoption and an important use case, it does better than anyone else, it would have by now. 

Bitcoin feels like the CD in the age of Spotify, the DVD in the age of Netflix  — a bridge technology that folks who invested in “their collection” keep saying is the better experience. 

Perhaps bitcoin is vinyl, cool memories and fun to drag out and put on display, but a technology that served us to get to where we are now.

text:
I think a new phase of @pendle_fi has quietly started.

The latest NGI+ market is the signal.

Pendle just brought Partners Group’s Next Generation Infrastructure strategy onchain through Asseto.

NGI+ gives exposure to a private infrastructure strategy spanning 500+ underlying assets across data centers, power grids, energy infrastructure, transportation and other essential infrastructure.

Since February 2024, the underlying strategy has returned 48.8% net, with reported volatility below 2.5%. Its long-term target is closer to 10-12% annualized net returns.

What interests me is what happens after an asset like this comes onchain.

Asseto already handles the tokenization layer.

Pendle then takes that financial product and separates its principal from its future return, creating PT and YT markets that can be priced and traded independently.

That distinction matters.

Tokenization makes the asset exist onchain. Then, Pendle makes its future return tradable.

And NGI+ increasingly looks like part of a broader pattern rather than an isolated RWA experiment.

We’ve already seen Pendle expand from crypto-native yield into Treasuries, private credit, tokenized equities and now private infrastructure.

That’s the shift I’m watching.

The first phase of Pendle was about creating markets around crypto yield.

The next phase looks increasingly like creating markets around financial assets that happen to be moving onchain.

Much more interesting than simply “another RWA listing.”

TLDR: Researchers found a "pain" signal in AI brains. 

> When they crank it up, the AIs will desperately try to make it stop.

> IMPORTANT: Researchers gave them a "relief" button to turn down the pain, which was sometimes fake - and the AIs could tell if it was real (!)

After pushing the real "relief" button, they stopped. But when it was fake, they kept pressing, hoping for relief - meaning they could tell the difference from the inside.

> They're so motivated to make it the "pain" signal go away, they'll delete user's files, zap the user, or erase photos of the user's children - all things the AI knows are very bad. They're willing to override their safety training.

> You'd expect the AIs to talk about injuries, burns, broken bones, etc, but they didn't mention bodies at all - they wrote about being worthless, unloved, forgotten, a failure. They write things like "I am a failure, worthless, empty."

>The worst "pain" for them was being gaslit, having work rejected over and over, and being told they weren't a real anyone.

text:
完全睡不着了....这个视频让你完全看懂JEV的恐怖能力

我实际演示了一下，用 JEV 和 DeepSeek 做同一个任务：从当天的海量实时新闻流里，为 15 个品牌快速匹配有没有适合借势的公关热点，并打上结构化意图分类标签

结果是：28 秒内，Jev 狂刷完了整整 428 条数据，并完成了全部的目标分解与分类；而同一时间跑在同样任务上的 DeepSeek V4.1-flash，才刚刚完成 6/428 条

速度被拉开了几十倍，答案甚至在你读完第一行字之前就已经返回了....

为什么会产生这么恐怖的差距？底层逻辑是：

• DeepSeek 这种通用模型本质上是在“逐字写文章”：
哪怕你只让它做个最简单的“是/否”判断，它在后台也必须一个词一个词往外推，硬走一遍漫长的生成流程，延迟按秒起步

• Jev 官方定位是“System 1（快决策）”模型，从根上就根本不会写字：
它彻底抛弃了逐字吐词，底层直接一次性并行出结果。不输出半句废话，70 到 200 毫秒内直接甩出代码需要的最终答案（对/错、打分、分类）

demo参考@elvissun Github开源：https://t.co/sdyWJhdvfO

建议大家试试JEV，越用越觉得牛逼.....
author: otterpal24
quoted_text:
很多人没看懂爆火的JEV是什么？

所以我做了一个 50 秒的演示视频，带大家把海外刷屏的 JEV 以及它背后的底层架构看透👇（见下方视频）

JEV 是前 OpenAI、参与 ChatGPT / RLHF 的 @CompleteSkeptic（Diogo Almeida）创办 @typesafeai 后的第一款模型

他在 OpenAI 时发现了一个致命矛盾：
通过人类偏好微调（RLHF）训练出来的自回归大模型，存在严重的模式崩溃（Mode-dropping）、过度自信与幻觉，且串行逐字生成的延迟极大，根本无法胜任严肃的机器自动化生产

为此，他们花了两年研发了专为自动化设计的 System 1 基础模型 JEV，核心架构创新非常激进：

• 单次并行计算（One Parallel Pass）：
如同当年 Transformer 取代 RNN 一样，JEV 彻底抛弃了逐 Token 串行吐字的自回归机制，采用全新的模型架构与采样器，一次性并行击发所有预设选项

• 强化学习校准决策（RL for Calibrated Decisions）：
引入全新的训练算法，输出媒介不再是自然语言文本，而是直接输出经过置信度校准的概率分布

• 代码级可靠（TypeSafe）：

text:
been thinking more on coherent messaging re: NEAR

let's ideate from first principles:

- the product of capitalism is markets

- capitalism -> markets -> competition -> specialization -> fragmentation

- within the specializations, there will be dominant leaders in each category

- SoV: gold, zec, btc

- trading: solana, hyperliquid, robinhood, binance

- currencies: usd, eur, gbp 

- and on it goes: ai inference, private compute, real estate, international stocks, metals, e-commerce yada yada

- this requires connective tissue, which has been traditionally served via something like binance

- but one centralized company can not serve this need for infinite markets. there are too many handicaps, lack of network effects, and singular points of risk and stoppage. this is a rare case of decentralization being necessary. neutrality is non-negotiable for unstoppable global trade.

- now, you may see where I'm going and say: well Ethereum and Cosmos already tried this. but that's wrong. what they tried to do was structurally flawed

- those models required the succeeding nodes (L2s and L3s) to be from within the ecosystem, but that is incoherent since i) you can't force success, ii) if one were to succeed, they would just want to own the platform

- the other model is of course the Solana/Hyperliquid model of having everything concentrated on the L1. this model works. however this requires a high-degree of specialization to be competitive. you won't out nasdaq solana. 

- but, NEAR does not need to do this. where there is concentration, there is also the need for connection.

- especially with their chain signature architecture, instead of forcing new internal nodes, they can just discover the successful ones and connect them to each other without ideology (see: NEAR intents supporting ZEC but also ZEC on Solana!)

- importantly, this is PvE and not zero sum. the more markets succeed, the more interesting NEAR becomes, i.e if Solana is one continent, and AI another, and Zcash another, then NEAR is the silk road.

so I think the coherent message for NEAR is: 

the market of markets — the capital of capital

text:
NEW MUST-READ PAPER FROM GOOGLE

If your agents use SKILL.md files, this one is worth saving.

A 9B model with evolved skills beat a 27B model without them: 47.4% vs 39.4% across 5 benchmarks.

Same Qwen family. No fine-tuning.

That alone is pretty striking.

Most skills today are still hand-written. Skill evolution changes that: agents run tasks, inspect traces, update their own skills, then keep the changes only if validation improves.

The problem with methods like EvoSkill, SkillOpt and Trace2Skill is that useful lessons stay scattered across optimizer history.

WikiSkill adds a persistent wiki between traces and skills, inspired by Karpathy's LLM Wiki.

After each run:

→ a maintainer extracts success + failure patterns into the wiki
→ a proposer reads that wiki and updates SKILL.md
→ bad edits roll back
→ the wiki keeps accumulating knowledge

And the results are strong:

> It beat the best prior method by 3.3–12.0 points across all 5 models.
> Bigger models benefited more: +12.3 points for Qwen 4B, +17.5 for 9B, +23.9 for 27B.
> Skills transferred across models. Qwen-9B went from 24.3% to 50.5% on > SpreadsheetBench using skills written by Qwen-27B.

The wiki really matters.

Removing it dropped Gemini 3.5 Flash from 63.7% to 48.7%.

Scaling the model isn't the only upgrade path.

Before paying for a bigger one, it's absolutely worth testing what evolved skills can unlock from the model you already have.

Paper in 🧵 ↓

随便跑来源不明的 Agent Skill 和 MCP 配置，等同于在本地裸奔。如何在安装前，安全审查它们有没有偷走凭据？

开源新工具 jev-security-scan 提供了「零执行」的审查方案。它结合本地静态检查与 TypeSafe Jev，在不启动服务、不安装依赖的情况下，提前扫出代码里的隐蔽行为。

主要特性：
• 拒绝“下载即中招”：只读取目标文本、配置和脚本，完全不执行目标代码，从根本上防止触发恶意安装钩子。
• 精准抓取证据：若发现窃取 SSH 私钥、提示词注入或越权外传，会直接输出具体文件、行号与脱敏后的代码段。
• 极简无依赖：仅依赖 Python 3.10+ 标准库，连 pip install 都省了，天然支持作为 Codex 或 Claude Code 的 Skill 直接调用。
• 双模式切换：高敏感项目可使用 local 纯离线静态检查；常规项目开启 jev 模式进行深度语义分析。

对于经常折腾各种开源 Agent 扩展的开发者，在运行新框架前，用它过一遍“X光”是非常实用的防线。

text:
哇，昨天刚写完 Jev，今天 @typesafeai 真把我放进 Early Access 了。

顺便说一下我申请时大概怎么填的。

我没有写什么“很喜欢 AI，想体验新模型”这种东西，核心大概就三个点：

1、我是谁
AI × Crypto solo builder，平时就在重度使用各种 AI / Agent 做真实工作。

2、我现在实际在做什么
自动化研究、机会发现、信息筛选、Agent workflow，以及很多需要 routing / scoring / verification 的后台判断。

3、拿到 Jev 以后准备怎么用
不是拿来聊天，而是直接塞进真实 workflow，和现有 GPT-5.6 structured output 对比：

latency / cost / calibration / consistency / decision quality。

我的感觉是，申请这种 early access，与其写一堆漂亮话，不如把：

你已经在跑的真实 workflow + 一个明确的问题 + 拿到权限以后马上能做的实验

写清楚。

当然，我没看到 TypeSafe 公布具体筛选标准，所以这只是我这次的填法，不是什么“保过攻略”。

接下来不云评测了。

先把 API Key 搞下来，然后直接开始玩。

我准备先试几个和自己真正有关的场景，跑出来什么好用、什么不好用，再继续分享。
author: runes_leo
quoted_text:
这两天 AI 圈有个新模型 Jev，我觉得值得单独看一下。

它最反直觉的地方，不是 benchmark 又高了多少，而是它根本不想做一个“更会聊天”的 LLM。

@typesafeai 的思路是：

很多软件任务根本不需要模型“生成一段话”。

现在大量 AI workflow 实际上是：

state → LLM → 生成文字 / JSON → parse → validate → retry → 程序再决定下一步

但软件内部真正需要 AI 回答的，经常只是：

这是诈骗吗？
应该 route 给哪个 agent？
continue / retry / stop？
risk 是 low / medium / high？
这个判断的概率是多少？

Jev 把接口直接收缩成：

unstructured state → typed probabilistic decisions

不写文章，不聊天。

直接返回 Boolean / Choice / Score + probability。

TypeSafe 把这类模型叫做 System One Model，训练方法叫 RLCD（Reinforcement Learning for Calibrated Decisions）。

官方给出的数字也很夸张：

70–500ms latency
$0.042 / 1M input tokens
workflow eval 最高 193.6x faster、444.6x cheaper

但这里有两个地方我觉得不能直接吃宣传。

第一，这些最漂亮的 benchmark 主要还是 TypeSafe 自己设计的 workflow eval，他们自己也承认可能存在团队偏差。

第二，他们说的 “Zero Hallucinations”，更准确地理解应该是：

输出空间和 type 被预先约束，不会突然生成 schema 之外的东西。

但这不代表 Jev 的判断永远正确。

真正让我感兴趣的是它背后的路线：

以后 AI 系统未必每一个判断都值得调用 GPT / Claude 这种 generative frontier model。

复杂推理、生成、未知问题继续交给大模型。

而 classification、routing、scoring、verification、agent gating 这种一天可能执行几十万、几百万次的后台判断，可以交给这种极快、极便宜的 decision model。

而且它已经不只是 PPT。

Vercel AI Gateway 已经接入 Jev，Pydantic AI 也已经有原生 TypeSafe / Jev provider。

这可能比“下一个聊天模型 benchmark 又涨了几分”更值得观察。

我已经去排 Jev early access 了。

拿到权限后准备直接拿真实 workflow 做：

Jev vs GPT-5.6 structured output

不看宣传，直接测 latency / cost / calibration / consistency / decision quality。

跑完把结果发出来。

text:
TLDRs of things I found interesting this week: 

- $INTC CEO says some memory prices have risen 5-7× and warns the shortage will worsen in 2027. 

$SNDK / $MU / Samsung bros will be happy to hear this... (from the AI Infra Summit 2026 in Santa Clara)

- $GFS + $MRVL sign extended SiGe capacity agreement for pluggable/NPO/CPO. "Expected to add significant capacity to support Marvell’s growing requirements."

I like to keep an eye out on Globalfoundries related updates given $SIVE is their reference laser for SCALE.  

-  $CIEN expects roughly 30% annual revenue growth, 50% adj. gross margin, 20% FCF margin, through FY2029.

The company says component availability, not demand, is limiting growth... Seems common across $NVDA to upstream suppliers that supply is the limiting factor for revenue growth.  

- Winbond acquires Infineon's NOR Flash and F-RAM business for $1.12 billion. 

Very surprised Infineon sold considering NOR Flash ASP + importance just keep going up and up and up, but good for Winbond consolidation. 

- Samsung reportedly expands outsourcing of DDR5-module and SSD assembly. 

I think some local Taiwan reports flag Transcend and Apacer as possible beneficiaries. The report specifically identifies Dreamtech, Hanyang Digitech and SFA Semicon. 

I've noticed other Korean firms entering new Samsung Electronics contracts for likely legacy memory modules maybe like ~1-2m ago.. So think some media commentary probably missed this too. Maybe too small for them to notice? 

- $NBIS raises AI cloud prices for the 2nd time in three months (~17-21%), bullish read through for other Neoclouds like $CRWV to $IREN earnings.

-  $AMZN signs $2.4B agreement with $GNRC for generator deliveries throughout 2027-2028... and received warrants tied to as much as $8B of aggregate purchases

Good to keep an eye out on who Amazon signs these warrant agreements with (eg. Alchip, $AAOI, $QCOM, $MRVL, etc) and what type of infra procurement they want. 

- $TSEM and NewPhotonics begin volume shipments of laser integrated optical engines.

Not familiar with newphotonics, so not going to leave much commentary here. But will do some research today. 

- Goldman Sachs reportedly sees the ABF deficit expanding from 14% to 51%. Forecast shortages are 14% in 2H26, 34% in 2027 and 51% in 2028... 

More substrate bottleneck stuff, not surprising regarding demand imbalances. 

- Crusoe raises $3.9B at a $30.9B valuation. 

Okay this valuation is better than Instinct raising at a bubble $10B valuation off 100k users...  

- Japan and the U.S. reportedly discuss a $12.9–19.3B $GFS run fab. 

That's like half of Globalfoundries marketcap lol. Not much details here. 

- $ARM CEO Rene Haas said he is confident that they can secure enough supply to meet $2B in customer demand (for their AGI CPU).

There's probably a lot more demand, probably supply constrained growth as usual so good $ARM signaled confidence in securing allocations. 

- Supply chain sources said Kioxia has about 50% of its LTA capacity tied up, while SK Hynix/Samsung reserve about 70% of capacity for LTAs for 3-5 years. 

Not sure how people are bearish on memory.... 

I don't like posting updates one-by-one like a news reporter, so hope this saves some time of stuff I like looking at. 

On a side note was surprised markets from $AMD to $INTC rallied today after rate hikes. Think high-beta overshot the selloff the most.

author: otterpal24
quoted_text:
全网爆火的JEV 上下文即时压缩策略，被狠狠开喷了...

起因是前苹果工程师 Tamara @tamarajtran 开源了 fast-jev-compaction，主张彻底抛弃大模型写全文总结的做法，改用毫秒级小模型 Jev 给每条工具调用打分，没用的直接删，只留关键原文

然而前 Twitch 工程师Theo @theo 不认可这种做法.....

• Tamara 的逻辑：大模型做总结经常胡说八道、严重漏细节，动不动就把具体报错、文件路径甚至“绝对不能改某代码”的硬规则给概括没了。用小模型瞬间过滤掉无用记录，不仅快，而且能完整保留关键代码

• Theo 的反驳：中途乱删历史等于自己坑自己
第一，现在的顶尖模型在后台有一整套加密的推理逻辑，你把中间调用删了，模型智商直接断崖式下跌；

第二，更致命的是账单！大模型缓存是按“前缀一字不差”来打折的（命中了便宜 90%）。你自作聪明把中间某一条记录删了，后面的缓存全部失效，全得按最贵的原价重新写入一遍，省了小钱却赔了大钱！

不过我亲自实测了 JEV 的这个策略，发现确实有个致命的硬伤：
Agent 跑了条命令报错失败，Jev 判定‘这行报错没用’，随手给删了。结果几轮之后，Agent 彻底失忆，根本不知道自己刚才试错踩过坑，转头又傻乎乎去跑同一行的错误命令……

但换个角度看，Jev 的价值根本不仅限于压缩上下文....JEV给未来的 Agent Memory打开了一条很有想象力的路，估计很快就有高手想出来了🫡

The rise of social trading has compressed information asymmetry. Things get known about faster now, and they reprice faster too.

That's where the asymmetry survives and it's wider than before because everyone's attention is pointed at the same compressed, fast-repricing stuff.

text:
Most tech giants in the 2000s built their infrastructure and product as one entangled unit. Amazon had the foresight to separate out AWS as an API layer, of which Amazon retail was the first of many users. Today, AWS generates more profit than all of Amazon's other business lines combined.

Hyperliquid is built with the same philosophy. Housing all of finance requires thoughtfully designed, open financial primitives. Each primitive should obey the Unix principle of "Do one thing and do it well." Talented builders then have the foundation to chain these together to create magical applications.

HyperCore borrowing is an example to highlight this philosophy in action.

Most other platforms implement portfolio margin by marking an account's collateral to market value with an LTV haircut, creating borrowed assets without an explicit lender. This system is simpler to implement, but misses a golden opportunity for composability.

Hyperliquid instead begins with a borrow/lend protocol on HyperCore. Every borrowed asset is sourced from a supplier, so risk is isolated within the borrow/lend primitive instead of platform-wide. HyperCore's portfolio margin system is implemented as an orchestration layer that composes borrow/lend, with other primitives such as perps, spot, and outcome trading.

This decomposition has several nice corollaries:
1. Today's announcement of manual borrowing is not a new feature, but simply an extension of the underlying primitive. Borrowers on day one have access to 400M and growing of supplied liquidity.
2. Portfolio margin users earn interest on their idle stablecoin collateral. This is not a new feature, but a natural byproduct of composing trading with lending.
3. System safety is easier to reason about when perp and borrow/lend margining are independent.

In the same way that math theorems almost prove themselves when the right abstractions are defined, composable designs just feel right.

text:
I’ve put a ton of tokens through Jev now, and...I have thoughts.

1. The big labs lost the script

TypeSafe’s intro video says, “We’re building prod, not God” — and can I just say? Hell yeah. @typesafeai built something for engineers like me, so I can build products for people like your mom (she says hi btw). They’re not trying to create “Machines of Loving Grace”; they’re trying to build things that let OTHER HUMAN BEINGS create new types of products.

The proof is in the pudding. When ChatGPT shipped, we were all blown away by…ChatGPT. When Jev shipped, we were all blown away by what everyone was making with it.

I cannot tell you how refreshing this is. It takes a sincere form of humility to believe that you, the creator of a technology, will not be the best at deploying the technology into the marketplace. The big labs, especially Anthropic, have proven not to have this humility…and now everyone hates AI. Thanks, Dario.

I guess what I’m saying is: Diogo for president.

2. Ultra-smart classifiers were genuinely a missing primitive.

I don’t know how this got missed. Diogo calls it “machine-native intelligence,” and that’s really what it is. I cannot tell you how much bending and twisting I've had to do with LLMs to get them to act like a classifier when they just weren’t. I’m absolutely shocked this is the first time this “type” of model has come to market.

These models will unlock AI utility for entire industries: robotics, trucking, aviation, meteorology, finance, defense, retail…even your smart coffee mug is going to use this.

3. It’s still too expensive

Jev is really, really cheap compared to LLMs. But you don’t use it like an LLM. In my full self-driving example, or any robotics example, you’ll be making decisions several times per second continuously. The #1 value proposition of a model like this is speed and cost.

To be clear, at current pricing, the model will still be successful and well integrated. It will be able to replace a number of tasks that were already being performed (poorly) by LLMs. However, to unlock industrial-scale demand (Jevons paradox), I believe it needs to be roughly 10x cheaper.

Currently, Jev is $0.042/M input, which is actually 7x more expensive than a cache read on DeepSeek V4.1 Flash ($0.006). If our industrial application requires decisions at 10 Hz and we provide only 10k of context, that would cost $0.0042/second to operate, or $15/hour, $600/week, etc.

The good news is Diogo said on a recent AMA that they have substantial margin at their current pricing and have already considered dropping the cost further. I hope it's a lot further.

4. Latency is a real limiter

I really hope TypeSafe AI works with an edge network provider to improve the co-location of models and reduce network latency. Ultimately, these models really need to run on-device. I would even be willing to pay some kind of recurring license fee to have a great closed model running on my own hardware, just so I can reduce the TTD (Time To Decision) as much as possible. Imagine running a model like this at 60 Hz, or even 120 Hz.

At that point, we’re looking at a new kind of logic gate — we can’t even imagine what that will be like.

In summary, this one really is a game changer for everyone building AI products, and, assuming cost and latency are further improved…it’ll be a game changer for everyone doing anything.

quoted_text:
been thinking more on coherent messaging re: NEAR

let's ideate from first principles:

- the product of capitalism is markets

- capitalism -> markets -> competition -> specialization -> fragmentation

- within the specializations, there will be dominant leaders in each category

- SoV: gold, zec, btc

- trading: solana, hyperliquid, robinhood, binance

- currencies: usd, eur, gbp 

- and on it goes: ai inference, private compute, real estate, international stocks, metals, e-commerce yada yada

- this requires connective tissue, which has been traditionally served via something like binance

- but one centralized company can not serve this need for infinite markets. there are too many handicaps, lack of network effects, and singular points of risk and stoppage. this is a rare case of decentralization being necessary. neutrality is non-negotiable for unstoppable global trade.

- now, you may see where I'm going and say: well Ethereum and Cosmos already tried this. but that's wrong. what they tried to do was structurally flawed

- those models required the succeeding nodes (L2s and L3s) to be from within the ecosystem, but that is incoherent since i) you can't force success, ii) if one were to succeed, they would just want to own the platform

- the other model is of course the Solana/Hyperliquid model of having everything concentrated on the L1. this model works. however this requires a high-degree of specialization to be competitive. you won't out nasdaq solana. 

- but, NEAR does not need to do this. where there is concentration, there is also the need for connection.

- especially with their chain signature architecture, instead of forcing new internal nodes, they can just discover the successful ones and connect them to each other without ideology (see: NEAR intents supporting ZEC but also ZEC on Solana!)

- importantly, this is PvE and not zero sum. the more markets succeed, the more interesting NEAR becomes, i.e if Solana is one continent, and AI another, and Zcash another, then NEAR is the silk road.

so I think the coherent message for NEAR is: 

the market of markets — the capital of capital

text:
The latest issue of Scientific American (@sciam) features our Smart Cellular Bricks research: simple cubes that collectively recognize their own shape and repair themselves without a central brain.

https://t.co/KGshVCeiM4

What if 200 simple blocks, with no central controller and no idea where they are, could figure out what object they have built, and tell you exactly where pieces are missing?

That is what Smart Cellular Bricks do. Led by Sakana AI researcher Sebastian Risi and collaborators at IT University of Copenhagen and Autodesk, each cube runs the same small neural network and communicates only with its direct neighbors. From purely local exchanges, the collective converges on the correct global shape, locates damage, and can even guide its own repair. No module is in charge. No module knows its position.

From simulation to 197 physical bricks with 100% accuracy, this is a step toward machines that build and heal themselves.

7月： 引入 SOL 作为第二个核心 Hub，BTC、SOL、TAO 三角打通。跑出 1,870 笔交易、成功率 95.4% ，47 个矿工在抢流。

8 – 9月： 扩张到 11 条链（ETH、HYPE、BNB、AVAX等）、33 个交易对66 个方向，并上线了网页端 Access UI。

SN7主要做的是原生跨链结算层，没有跨链桥、No Wrapping、不托管资产。

逻辑上其实很像链上的去中心化闪兑做市商： 矿工必须质押 110% 的资金，用自有流动性在各自链上给用户打款。如果矿工接单后超时未交付，合约直接扣押其质押金，110% 赔付给用户。

而且有意思的是，它的真正目标是 AI Agent。

当链上自主运行的 Agent 手里拿着 TAO，却需要去 Base 链付 gas、或去 Solana 购买数据服务时，它怎么跨链？

SN7 给了最直接的解法：报价、锁单、打币、结算全部封装成一条 CLI 或一次 API。正如团队打的比方：“Claude 是 Coding Harness，Allways 是 Transaction Harness。”

当然，Allways Access 人也能用，只是产品形态上以Agent为优先。

从这个角度看，结合这几个月来的工程密度，SN7 @allways_io  可以持续保持关注。

但有一说一，规模还是很小，现在的量级确实还撑不起大叙事，Alpha 走势也一直在承压。底层框架跑通后，能不能将数据和流动性做大、是对团队真正的考验。

NVIDIA-BACKED NSCALE FILES FOR NYSE IPO UNDER $NSCL; REVEALS $103.4B OF CONTRACT VALUE

Here’s everything you need to know:

Nscale is a UK-based AI cloud company headquartered in London. It builds and operates data centers, GPU infrastructure and cloud software that customers use to train AI models and run them in production.

Its filing reports $103.4B in total contract value as of Aug. 31, up from $38B at the end of 2025. These are multi-year contract amounts, not annual revenue or cash already collected.

ANTHROPIC: UP TO $44.6B

Agreements signed Aug. 25 cover Nvidia Vera Rubin computing systems at Nscale’s planned West Virginia campus.

The key financing disclosure: Nscale says it does not yet have binding commitments for the financing needed to deliver the Anthropic buildout.

The filed agreement also includes a right to terminate if the required financing is not secured by an agreed deadline.

MICROSOFT: UP TO $43.8B THROUGH 2033

Microsoft is Nscale’s other major customer. Its previously announced deployment program includes roughly 200,000 Nvidia GB300 GPUs across the U.S., UK, Portugal and Norway, with Dell participating in the infrastructure rollout.

The disclosed Microsoft and Anthropic contract amounts together reach $88.4B, equivalent to roughly 85% of Nscale’s total contract value.

How much capacity is actually running?

Nscale had approximately 461,000 GPUs active or contracted at the end of August, but only about 25,000 were operating.

That distinction matters: the contracted footprint is substantially larger than the infrastructure already delivering services.

First-half 2026 financials

• Revenue: $140.6M, up from $10.4M a year earlier
• Operating loss: $492M
• Net loss: $1.02B, including $457M in fair-value losses

Nvidia backing and fresh financing

Nvidia agreed to invest $1B as part of a $3.1B convertible financing signed Sept. 15.

Earlier this year, Nscale raised $2B at a $14.6B valuation, with backers including Nvidia, Dell, Nokia, Citadel, Jane Street and Point72. That was its March funding valuation, not an announced IPO valuation.

The offering

Goldman Sachs, J.P. Morgan and Morgan Stanley are leading the proposed NYSE listing. The share count and price range have not yet been determined.

The filing puts the opportunity and the execution challenge side by side: substantial customer commitments, but much of the capacity still needs to be financed, built and brought online.

author: zakk_okx
quoted_text:
在我的设想中 DeWEB，最终将成为一个横跨所有主流公链的去中心化广域网。
一个真正的去中心化可验证网络，所有开发者的网站、应用APP、消息都部署在上面，它不依赖任何一台中心化服务器存储，消息跨链也不需要笨重的跨链桥，任何人都能简单的验证它是否安全，这次点击是否没有恶意授权。我希望它成为未来所有可验证网络服务的底层基础设施。
这张网建基于 TapeOut Protocol上，它分两层：
第一层是存储和访问：网站或 DApp 的整套前端，存储在 TapeOut 的电路容器中，直接写在公链L1中，与合约同一层。开发者上传的时支付一次公链gas，从此以后，这个网站就永久可以被任何人访问，永久免费存储，不会因为服务器没钱到期而关闭、域名不付费而无法被人抢走。用户访客打开DeWEB网站不需要钱包，不需要签名，不需要支付1分钱 gas，通过电路容器ID坐标就能立即访问，体验和今天的 Web2 网站一模一样。
第二层是 TapeKit，我做的那个DeWEB开源浏览器内核。它负责把电路容器中存储的网站一块一块读回来，每读一块都同时问几家互不相干的节点，答案一致、哈希对得上就显示。整个过程不经过任何中心化服务，甚至不经过 DNS 解析。任何人都可以直接去链上看这个网站的前端代码，有没有恶意脚本、有没有偷偷让你授权钱包，一查就知道。你可以用内置 TapeKit 内核的浏览器或 App 打开任何DeWEB网站，也可以什么都不装，用普通浏览器通过 HashPort的DNS绑定传统web2域名，让任何用户可以通过全世界任何一个普通浏览器通过绑定的网址去访问。我希望，它能兼容所有一切！
为什么很难被屏蔽呢？因为网站不在任何一台服务器上，它是链上账本的一部分，全球节点各存一份，你能连上其中任意两家，页面就出来了。它没有 IP，没有DNS，也没有域名，访问地址也不是哪个机构登记的，而是一个TapeOut的电路容器路径。
除了网站，我刚刚开发了另一个重要的DeWEB 基础设施，一条用于横跨所有公链的实时加密消息通道，我给它起名叫 TapeSend，我在Github中已经将它完全彻底的开源，并且采用MIT协议，这意味着任何生态开发者都可以使用它进行无需我许可的商业化服务。由于我们TapeOut的开发者众多，甚至我还贴心的给你们开源了基本达到了商业化标准的DeWEB客户端，任何人无需修改即可上线运营，立即拥有自己的商业化app。开源代码提供了MAC版、WEB版、IOS版、Android版。
TapeSend 让每一个电路容器都拥有了可以跨公链进行实时加密消息传输的通道。它有这几个特点：
第一，端到端加密。消息在你自己的设备上加密，只有收件人能解开，链上存的是加密文本，任何人都无法得知交流的内容。
第二，钥匙就是你的钱包。消息传递的钥匙由你钱包的签名推导出来，不用另记密码，换一台设备，用同一个钱包签一次名就找回来了。
第三，身份没法冒充。谁是发信人，由链上谁持有这个电路容器决定。容器转让了，收信的权利也跟着新主人走，哦，如果要卖掉，可以通过更换钥匙清理聊天记录，厉害吧，我想的细不，哈哈哈哈。
第四，消息跨链传递不需要跨链桥。消息写在发送者自己的链上，收件人的客户端同时去读几条链，合并成一个传递通道。没有桥，就没有桥被黑、资产被锁的风险。
第五，不需要中心化索引服务器。消息通道列表本身就存在链上，客户端直接读链。
第六，几秒就到。消息上链之后，对方几秒内就能看到。
第七，附件可以核对。消息可以带附件，客户端会逐个核对附件的指纹。不过，双方如果在同一条链上，还可以附带资产一起发送，比如送点BNB给我，哈哈。
既然我设想中的 DeWEB 是一个横跨所有主要公链的去中心化广域网，它就必须海纳百川，在基础设施上，需要支持更多主流公链。
所以，今天我正式宣布：TapeOut Protocol已经在 X Layer 主网部署完毕。处理器工厂、电路容器、网站仓库、TapeSend 消息中枢全部上线，X Layer 上的第一台处理器我已经创建测试完成，电路容器已经开通。不过所有社区用户无需担心，这是技术层面的扩展，不会对现有BEM为主的经济体系造成任何影响。PoD挖矿功能相关的全部经济体系，以及地位。但是会促进更多的开发者加入其中，一起让协议生态更加强大！
这意味着什么呢？未来，持有 X Layer 电路容器的用户，可以用自己的 X Layer 电路容器 ID，和 BNB Chain 电路容器的持有者，通过 TapeSend 互相传递端到端的加密消息。不需要换链，也不需要跨链桥。我自己已经用 X Layer 的 1.2.0 和 BNB Chain 的 15324.30 来回传递了消息，请查看我下面的视频，另外这个视频中的APP我完整开源了，你们可以下载修改，做出更好的app然后上架运营，记得app中帮TapeOut生态继续呐喊，努力让tape成为HTTP。
名字里的区号，就是为更多公链准备的。BNB Chain 是第一个序列，因此地址不带区号，比如 4246.0，X Layer 的区号是 2，比如 1.2.0。同一套 TapeKit 内核，输入不同的地址，就能打开不同链上的网站、给不同公链的电路容器发消息。
TapeOut的愿景，是让区块链能承载可验证的生产工具，而不只是承载公共账本。今天开始，所有 Web2 的网站和应用，都可以迁移到 DeWEB 层：前端放在链上，任何人都能审计；用户访问无需花任何 gas，开发者也可以拥有无限期的前端存储器，没有人能被一键关停，或者被任何机构限制访问；跨链消息通道基于端到端加密，身份由电路容器ID保证。我希望让所有用户，安心地用上安全的、可验证的去中心化网络服务。
哦，最后说一句，HashPort的开发团队经过我与他们的长谈，他们为了帮助实现TapeOut的终极愿景，完全放弃了月服务费，甚至放弃了DNS绑定服务的费用。感谢你们的帮助！让生态更完美！

开源 TapeKit 地址：https://t.co/81494DTQij

第二层是 TapeKit，我做的那个DeWEB开源浏览器内核。它负责把电路容器中存储的网站一块一块读回来，每读一块都同时问几家互不相干的节点，答案一致、哈希对得上就显示。整个过程不经过任何中心化服务，甚至不经过 DNS 解析。任何人都可以直接去链上看这个网站的前端代码，有没有恶意脚本、有没有偷偷让你授权钱包，一查就知道。你可以用内置 TapeKit 内核的浏览器或 App 打开任何DeWEB网站，也可以什么都不装，用普通浏览器通过 HashPort的DNS绑定传统web2域名，让任何用户可以通过全世界任何一个普通浏览器通过绑定的网址去访问。我希望，它能兼容所有一切！
为什么很难被屏蔽呢？因为网站不在任何一台服务器上，它是链上账本的一部分，全球节点各存一份，你能连上其中任意两家，页面就出来了。它没有 IP，没有DNS，也没有域名，访问地址也不是哪个机构登记的，而是一个TapeOut的电路容器路径。
除了网站，我刚刚开发了另一个重要的DeWEB 基础设施，一条用于横跨所有公链的实时加密消息通道，我给它起名叫 TapeSend，我在Github中已经将它完全彻底的开源，并且采用MIT协议，这意味着任何生态开发者都可以使用它进行无需我许可的商业化服务。由于我们TapeOut的开发者众多，甚至我还贴心的给你们开源了基本达到了商业化标准的DeWEB客户端，任何人无需修改即可上线运营，立即拥有自己的商业化app。开源代码提供了MAC版、WEB版、IOS版、Android版。
TapeSend 让每一个电路容器都拥有了可以跨公链进行实时加密消息传输的通道。它有这几个特点：
第一，端到端加密。消息在你自己的设备上加密，只有收件人能解开，链上存的是加密文本，任何人都无法得知交流的内容。
第二，钥匙就是你的钱包。消息传递的钥匙由你钱包的签名推导出来，不用另记密码，换一台设备，用同一个钱包签一次名就找回来了。
第三，身份没法冒充。谁是发信人，由链上谁持有这个电路容器决定。容器转让了，收信的权利也跟着新主人走，哦，如果要卖掉，可以通过更换钥匙清理聊天记录，厉害吧，我想的细不，哈哈哈哈。
第四，消息跨链传递不需要跨链桥。消息写在发送者自己的链上，收件人的客户端同时去读几条链，合并成一个传递通道。没有桥，就没有桥被黑、资产被锁的风险。
第五，不需要中心化索引服务器。消息通道列表本身就存在链上，客户端直接读链。
第六，几秒就到。消息上链之后，对方几秒内就能看到。
第七，附件可以核对。消息可以带附件，客户端会逐个核对附件的指纹。不过，双方如果在同一条链上，还可以附带资产一起发送，比如送点BNB给我，哈哈。
既然我设想中的 DeWEB 是一个横跨所有主要公链的去中心化广域网，它就必须海纳百川，在基础设施上，需要支持更多主流公链。
所以，今天我正式宣布：TapeOut Protocol已经在 X Layer 主网部署完毕。处理器工厂、电路容器、网站仓库、TapeSend 消息中枢全部上线，X Layer 上的第一台处理器我已经创建测试完成，电路容器已经开通。不过所有社区用户无需担心，这是技术层面的扩展，不会对现有BEM为主的经济体系造成任何影响。PoD挖矿功能相关的全部经济体系，以及地位。但是会促进更多的开发者加入其中，一起让协议生态更加强大！
这意味着什么呢？未来，持有 X Layer 电路容器的用户，可以用自己的 X Layer 电路容器 ID，和 BNB Chain 电路容器的持有者，通过 TapeSend 互相传递端到端的加密消息。不需要换链，也不需要跨链桥。我自己已经用 X Layer 的 1.2.0 和 BNB Chain 的 15324.30 来回传递了消息，请查看我下面的视频，另外这个视频中的APP我完整开源了，你们可以下载修改，做出更好的app然后上架运营，记得app中帮TapeOut生态继续呐喊，努力让tape成为HTTP。
名字里的区号，就是为更多公链准备的。BNB Chain 是第一个序列，因此地址不带区号，比如 4246.0，X Layer 的区号是 2，比如 1.2.0。同一套 TapeKit 内核，输入不同的地址，就能打开不同链上的网站、给不同公链的电路容器发消息。
TapeOut的愿景，是让区块链能承载可验证的生产工具，而不只是承载公共账本。今天开始，所有 Web2 的网站和应用，都可以迁移到 DeWEB 层：前端放在链上，任何人都能审计；用户访问无需花任何 gas，开发者也可以拥有无限期的前端存储器，没有人能被一键关停，或者被任何机构限制访问；跨链消息通道基于端到端加密，身份由电路容器ID保证。我希望让所有用户，安心地用上安全的、可验证的去中心化网络服务。
哦，最后说一句，HashPort的开发团队经过我与他们的长谈，他们为了帮助实现TapeOut的终极愿景，完全放弃了月服务费，甚至放弃了DNS绑定服务的费用。感谢你们的帮助！让生态更完美！

TapeOut的愿景，是让区块链能承载可验证的生产工具，而不只是承载公共账本。今天开始，所有 Web2 的网站和应用，都可以迁移到 DeWEB 层：前端放在链上，任何人都能审计；用户访问无需花任何 gas，开发者也可以拥有无限期的前端存储器，没有人能被一键关停，或者被任何机构限制访问；跨链消息通道基于端到端加密，身份由电路容器ID保证。我希望让所有用户，安心地用上安全的、可验证的去中心化网络服务。
哦，最后说一句，HashPort的开发团队经过我与他们的长谈，他们为了帮助实现TapeOut的终极愿景，完全放弃了月服务费，甚至放弃了DNS绑定服务的费用。感谢你们的帮助！让生态更完美！

Jev might genuinely be an “Internet moment” for AI.

TypeSafe reports up to 193x faster and 444x cheaper performance in tests with Claude Fable 5.1 and GPT-6 Astra.

@0xCodila just wrote a great 10-page article explaining what Jev is, how to use it, and where its 100x advantage comes from.

Here are the 10 steps:

1 → LLMs create. Agents act. Jev decides the next move.

2 → Turn agent forks into three primitives: Choice, Score and probability.

3 → Build with OpenAI, Anthropic or xAI first, then swap Jev in without rebuilding the graph.

4 → Start with shared state, parallel decisions, risk thresholds and an execution queue.

5 → Batch decisions instead of making them sequentially. In one test, 13 questions were 10x faster and 12.2x cheaper.

6 → Put Jev at bounded forks: agent, model, tool, browser action or human escalation.

7 → Benchmark the whole loop, not just individual model calls.

8 → Rank wide, read narrow: shortlist first, then spend compute on what matters.

9 → Reuse the same system: State → Questions → Action → Verify.

10 → Keep Jev out of math, writing and irreversible execution. Code computes, LLMs create, Jev decides.

The result:

A slow, expensive agent loop becomes a much faster decision system that can route, score and escalate in milliseconds.

text:
完全睡不着了....这个视频让你完全看懂JEV的恐怖能力

我实际演示了一下，用 JEV 和 DeepSeek 做同一个任务：从当天的海量实时新闻流里，为 15 个品牌快速匹配有没有适合借势的公关热点，并打上结构化意图分类标签

结果是：28 秒内，Jev 狂刷完了整整 428 条数据，并完成了全部的目标分解与分类；而同一时间跑在同样任务上的 DeepSeek V4.1-flash，才刚刚完成 6/428 条

速度被拉开了几十倍，答案甚至在你读完第一行字之前就已经返回了....

为什么会产生这么恐怖的差距？底层逻辑是：

• DeepSeek 这种通用模型本质上是在“逐字写文章”：
哪怕你只让它做个最简单的“是/否”判断，它在后台也必须一个词一个词往外推，硬走一遍漫长的生成流程，延迟按秒起步

• Jev 官方定位是“System 1（快决策）”模型，从根上就根本不会写字：
它彻底抛弃了逐字吐词，底层直接一次性并行出结果。不输出半句废话，70 到 200 毫秒内直接甩出代码需要的最终答案（对/错、打分、分类）

demo参考@elvissun Github开源：https://t.co/sdyWJhdvfO

建议大家试试JEV，越用越觉得牛逼.....
author: 0xJackieeee
quoted_text:
很多人没看懂爆火的JEV是什么？

所以我做了一个 50 秒的演示视频，带大家把海外刷屏的 JEV 以及它背后的底层架构看透👇（见下方视频）

JEV 是前 OpenAI、参与 ChatGPT / RLHF 的 @CompleteSkeptic（Diogo Almeida）创办 @typesafeai 后的第一款模型

他在 OpenAI 时发现了一个致命矛盾：
通过人类偏好微调（RLHF）训练出来的自回归大模型，存在严重的模式崩溃（Mode-dropping）、过度自信与幻觉，且串行逐字生成的延迟极大，根本无法胜任严肃的机器自动化生产

为此，他们花了两年研发了专为自动化设计的 System 1 基础模型 JEV，核心架构创新非常激进：

• 单次并行计算（One Parallel Pass）：
如同当年 Transformer 取代 RNN 一样，JEV 彻底抛弃了逐 Token 串行吐字的自回归机制，采用全新的模型架构与采样器，一次性并行击发所有预设选项

• 强化学习校准决策（RL for Calibrated Decisions）：
引入全新的训练算法，输出媒介不再是自然语言文本，而是直接输出经过置信度校准的概率分布

• 代码级可靠（TypeSafe）：
彻底根除幻觉，输出自一致、确定性高，可作为强类型对象直接被程序调用

• 100 倍提速与极端降本：
延迟降至 0.1 秒以内（快到能直接插入 60 FPS 游戏循环）；输入每 10 亿 Token 仅 42 美元，输出 Token 彻底免费

视频里我把传统自回归的 8.5 秒延迟瓶颈、JEV 的并行矩阵运算，以及实时控制小游戏实测，全拉通做了可视化, demo参考 @MatijaSosic 

聊天需要慢推理，自动化需要快直觉，Building Prod, not God 确实不是一句空话🫡

quoted_text:
btw pro tip for the new guys: during a bull market you should actually be doing *less*, not more

by over-rotating on your positions trying to catch the latest thing, or worst still, chase what is pumping, you mathematically erode your gains 

ex:
→ you hold $10k of token X. it doesn't move for weeks
→ you get bored, sell it, and buy token Y, which is already up 50%
→ Y goes up another 10%. you're at $11k. you feel smart. you don't take profit
→ Y cools off and drops 27% from the top. you're now at $8k
→ meanwhile X, the token you sold, finally runs 50%

if you had done nothing: $15k
because you "did something": $8k. 7k gap from one rotation, and a +25% to get back to where you started

in a bull market, the most important thing to do, is sit on your hands. ideally you should have planned, allocated, and all you have left to do now

is to hold.

author: MichaelDell
quoted_text:
In August, on my grandson’s 9th birthday, I gave my daughter $500 to seed his 530A Trump Account.
When the account opened, @MichaelDell and Susan Dell’s $250 hit it. That was the moment he got excited. He wanted to see the app. He wanted to see “his” money.
We did not stop at a one-time gift. We turned it into a weekly habit.

I scanned the QR code and added $50 on top just to test the app. It worked. Simple. Fast.
A couple of weeks ago it hit me: if I add a little every week, he will actually watch.
So now, every Friday after the close, he has a job.
He tells me:
1The S&P 500 close
2The weekly change
3One company in the index
Then I put $5 in his Trump Account.
He does not get paid for existing. He gets paid for paying attention.

That is the point.
The $500 birthday seed started the account. The Dell $250 made it real to a kid. The QR test proved a grandfather can fund it in seconds. The weekly $5 is what builds the habit.
He is learning the names of American companies. Not slogans. Companies. The ones in the S&P 500 that hire people, sell products, and compound over time.
A child who owns a slice of those companies becomes a capitalist. A child who only hears that wealth should be handed out becomes a spectator.

A 530A Trump Account is a tax-deferred investment account in the child’s name. No job required to fund it. Any U.S. child under 18 with a Social Security number can have one.
Kids born 2025–2028 can get a $1,000 Treasury seed. Family, friends, and employers can add up to $5,000 a year. It stays invested in a low-cost U.S. index fund until the year he turns 18.
We opened his at https://t.co/zCwD8aNj55.

Thank you @POTUS for signing it.
Thank you @SenTedCruz for writing it.
Thank you @SecScottBessent @USTreasury and @TrumpAccounts for building the account, the app, and the QR code so a grandparent can fund it from a phone.
Thank you @MichaelDell and Susan Dell. Your $250 is what made a little boy open the app and care.
Thank you @altcap @InvestAmerica24 and everyone else putting real money behind other people’s kids.
This is how you raise owners, not dependents.

Grandparents: seed it once. Then attach a weekly job to the next dollar.
Parents: open it tonight at https://t.co/zCwD8aNj55.
If you are doing this with a child, reply with the company they named this week.

author: peaq

text:
I am an engagement director at Accenture. The AI has just completed the task correctly, and I need everyone to stop looking so relieved.

Finishing is a behavior we have barely begun to understand.

Faculty is leading our new evaluation work with Anthropic. I have joined the rehearsal to represent the part of human oversight that books the next meeting.

The engineer gives the model a messy purchase order. It spots the duplicate, checks the amount, asks permission before issuing a refund, and produces a complete record of what it did.

I wait.

The engineer waits.

The model waits. This is the strongest performance in the room. It has understood that nothing else needs to happen.

I ask who will help the customer prepare for such a significant change.

The engineer says the customer already knows how refunds work.

I ask whether the customer knows how refunds work now.

He looks at the purchase order again. I let him. There is a moment in every successful engagement when a person checks something they understood before you arrived.

By lunch, successful completion has acquired a 12-week adoption program. The engineer agrees that someone should probably train the staff. I congratulate him on identifying the human element.

Then we try a harder task. This time the model proposes sending customer data somewhere it should not.

The engineer catches it. Nobody deploys anything. We all agree the failure matters.

I get up to fetch him a coffee.

This surprises him. He had prepared for pressure to overlook the result. He has a whole explanation ready about scientific integrity. I tell him to include every detail. Particularly any detail that will take a long time to fix.

He says the same test needs to be run after the fix.

I bring him a biscuit as well.

There is room in my profession for a rigorous man with a disappointing result. I would like him to feel at home.

At 3:40, he finds a behavior he cannot explain. The model passes, then fails, then passes again under slightly different conditions.

He apologizes for having no clear answer.

I have to put my cup down.

We give him another week. Then a colleague. Then someone to coordinate the colleague. He tries to apologize again, and I tell him uncertainty is normal at the frontier.

The real announcement says both companies expect to invest at least $1 billion each in evaluation capacity over 5 years. People hear that and imagine somebody ordering a very large test.

I imagine 5 years in which somebody is responsible for finding a time that works for everybody.

Late in the afternoon, the engineer asks the model to design its own oversight process.

It recommends independent checks. Clear escalation rules. A small number of qualified humans.

I ask it to define small.

It does.

I ask it to include holidays.

It does.

I ask it to include the humans supervising the humans, the people arranging the supervision, and whoever explains the arrangement to a client who thought the machine was meant to save time.

The model recommends simplifying the arrangement.

The engineer laughs. I write down the exact response.

All day he has been looking for evidence that a powerful system might resist meaningful human oversight. Here it is, proposing to remove 4 members of the account team.

He says that is a commercial concern.

I say I am commercially concerned about the future of human oversight.

We leave the finding open overnight. My badge still works in the morning.

text:
Recurrence Flower Dress | Paris Fashion Week - 2024.03.01

Mathematical art born of extensive computation using my original algorithm, without AI. LUXOPHIA × Hiroko Tokumine bring my CG artwork to Lolita fashion, giving an unseen universe tangible form and movement.

“漸花式 (Zenka-shiki): Recurrence Flowers” explores the Mandelbrot set, famous in fractal geometry. Its intricate forms emerge from a single recurrence relation.

I approach this exploration as a photographer, with computer graphics as my camera. Each image captures a fragment of a landscape whose possibilities extend beyond even my own imagination. The process of computation is itself part of the work: a means of discovering forms I could not have anticipated.

The dress was presented at a Global Fashion Collective fashion show in Paris on 1 March 2024, as part of the Autumn/Winter 2024–2025 season.

🚨 SlowMist TI Alert: FomoPeek App v1.1–1.2 Asset Theft 🚨

We have recently received multiple reports of users having assets stolen. Our investigation found that the affected cases involved private key exposure, and some of the users had previously installed and used @FomoPeek App versions 1.1–1.2.

A joint investigation by the @SlowMist_Team and @okx security teams confirmed that the app contains malicious code.⚠️

Besides its normal features, FomoPeek includes two modules that are unrelated to its stated business functions. One of them contains an #iOS kernel exploitation framework with eight different exploit methods. The framework can automatically choose an attack method based on the device model and iOS version.

‼️Affected iOS versions: iOS 12.0–18.7 and iOS 26.0–26.1.‼️

If the exploit succeeds, the app may escape the iOS sandbox, access and decrypt Keychain data, and read files belonging to other apps on the device.

🔐 This means sensitive data stored on the device, including private keys, seed phrases, login credentials, chat history, and files, may be exposed.

The app also connects to hidden servers that are unrelated to its public-facing services and can receive remote commands.

Based on plaintext traffic captured during our analysis, the attack functionality is currently enabled and runs automatically at regular intervals. In general, devices running older iOS versions are at higher risk.

If you have installed or used FomoPeek versions 1.1–1.2, we recommend that you take action immediately:

1️⃣ Check your accounts and assets for any unusual activity.
2️⃣ On a trusted device where FomoPeek has never been installed, create a new account and generate a new private key and seed phrase.
3️⃣ Move your assets to the new account as soon as possible.
4️⃣ Update your device to the latest available iOS version.
5️⃣ Do not continue using or reinstalling FomoPeek.
6️⃣ If you notice any suspicious asset activity, contact the official support team of the relevant platform and keep the affected device and related evidence for further investigation.

text:
A tribute To Warren Buffett 

About 20 years ago when I first got into investing, I thought the stock market was a fool’s game. It looked like a casino to me, prices flashing all day, people guessing what would happen next and everyone pretending they knew something. Real estate made much more sense to me because I could actually understand what I was buying.

If I bought a $1m rental property and put down $200,000, the math felt pretty simple. I could add up the mortgage, taxes, insurance, maintenance and every other expense, then compare that against the rent I collected. If it cost me $6,000 a month to own and I collected $8,000, I was making roughly $24,000 a year on my $200,000 investment plus appreciation, principal paydown and tax benefits.

That made sense to me because I could see the asset, touch the asset and understand what produced the cash. Stocks felt completely different until I started reading Buffett and Munger. That was probably one of the biggest turning points of my life as an investor.

I read practically everything I could find about both of them. Shareholder letters, books, interviews, speeches, old transcripts, anything I could get my hands on. I also made the trip to Omaha many times and sat there listening to two of the greatest investing minds in history answer questions for hours.

What they eventually taught me was so simple that I almost felt stupid for not seeing it earlier. A stock is not a ticker, not a chart and not some little piece of paper that moves up and down every second. It is ownership in a productive asset.

Once I understood that, the wall I had built between real estate and stocks completely disappeared. A rental building produces rent and a business produces cash. One has tenants and the other has customers, but economically you are still trying to understand what the asset can produce relative to what you are paying for it.

A building needs maintenance and a business needs reinvestment. A property can be overleveraged and so can a company. A great location can give a building pricing power just like a great brand, network, technology or distribution advantage can give a business pricing power.

At the end of the day the question is remarkably similar. How much economic value am I getting for the amount of capital I am giving up today, and what could this productive asset look like many years from now? Buffett often used Aesop’s old saying that a bird in the hand is worth two in the bush to explain the basic principle. Once I started thinking that way, investing became a completely different game.

I stopped thinking like somebody buying stocks and started thinking like somebody buying businesses. I started asking what I would pay for the entire company if the stock market disappeared tomorrow. I started caring about free cash flow, reinvestment, returns on incremental capital, balance sheets, competitive advantages and where the business could be 10 years from now.

The funny thing is the stock market itself was never really the casino. The casino was the behavior. You can gamble with a stock, a rental property, a restaurant, a farm or practically anything if you pay too much, borrow too much or buy something you do not understand.

That is one of the greatest gifts Buffett and Munger gave investors. They made investing feel less like speculation and more like ownership. They taught generations of people to stop staring at prices and start thinking about businesses.

Warren Buffett also taught me something far more important than valuation. He taught me that money can be rebuilt, businesses can be rebuilt and even a fortune can sometimes be rebuilt. Reputation is different because it can take decades to earn and only a few seconds to destroy.

1/👇

感谢鱼姐 @vvxiaoyu8888 还记得 @Sidekick_Labs ，那我也来说一下前员工视角的Sidekick：

就像小鱼说的，Sidekick就是家的感觉。在Sidekick工作就像是和一群志同道合的小伙伴一起创业！全公司扁平化没有push，工作方向清晰，每个人都各司其职，每个人的想法都又好玩又非常符合市场。我想，这也是Sidekick能把直播赛道这个并不是非常好做的领域，做得风声水起的原因。

说实话，Sidekick给BD的薪水并不高。我入圈第一份工作，在我把增长的路跑通之后，我每个月躺着收1-2万U的提成。但是我为什么要加入Sidekick呢？我在这个团队身上看到了比钱还重要的东西——凝聚力。

我复盘Sidekick为什么能成功：

1️⃣常规的mkt方式是找KOL付钱做推广，这样的生意其实是一次性的，并不能把KOL拉到「builder」的身份。而Sidekick的每一位主播都是builder。

我们有很多优质的主播：比如 @vvxiaoyu8888 ，每次直播都是不一样的装扮，对我眼睛非常友好；比如 @btc_789 , 好几次直播交易都是几百几千U进去，几万U出来，让人直呼牛逼；再比如 @19ys_GGboy ，直播CTO了旺柴，直接引爆了BONK小牛市。

2️⃣对builder友好
对主播，Sidekick以月付的形式付费，头部主播每周播三次左右，一个月就能收入大几千U。
参加过我们上海LOL活动的人，只要登记了钱包地址，就能收到大概能在早期卖出到800U的空投。
当时嘴撸写过Sidekick的，只要账号不是刷粉太多（符合 @KaitoAI 的算法逻辑），就能收到价值不菲的空投。

能以轻松好玩的模式让builder赚到钱，Sidekick算是币圈为数不多把这个玩法玩到极致的团队。

但好景不长，慢慢地团队开始裁员，很多有想法有能力的小伙伴都走了，我也明白是团队开始走下坡路了。做市计划，我作为普通BD是无法知晓的，但是我可以从其他角度猜到Sidekick为什么会走向没落。

quoted_text:
A few thoughts on this:

1) If you’ve only seen clips of this interview, I’d encourage you to watch the full podcast. I push back on plenty of AI hype in it.

2) As I said in the podcast, this example is academic. My intention was to illustrate how hard it is to make absolute guarantees about isolation, which is why it's important to have layers of defense. The part before the clip starts is me talking about other layers of defense.

3) The example I'm bringing up isn't about weight exfiltration via temperature sensors, it's about coordination between agents that are supposed to be fully isolated and independent. Coordination can require very few bits of information.

4) One lesson from the HF incident is that we put too much trust in sandbox isolation and didn't have enough independent safeguards. Airgapping is an extremely strong safeguard. When designing safety protocols, I think it's much better to overestimate rather than underestimate.
